findings.failure_path: SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP only appends to latched. While the main thread remains in cf.wait for up to 0.2 seconds, another worker can finish setup and enter run_agent: both ctx['stop'] and ctx['interrupted'] are still false, so it launches a new model process after the interrupt. Likewise, a signal delivered between calibration completion and this submission expression does not prevent samples from being submitted and launched. This violates the explicit no-run-after-interrupt requirement and permits additional spending after cancellation. The new tests leave the signalling child asleep and do not assert this concurrent launch boundary.
findings.smallest_fix: Make the signal latch visible to the worker and run_agent launch guards, and check it before submitting calibration or sample work. Add a synchronized regression that pauses a worker before spawn, delivers a signal, then releases the worker before the polling wait processes cancellation; assert that no model process starts.

concern_results.conclusion: Signal latching protects final evidence writes, but does not immediately prevent subsequent model launches.
Workers can initiate additional agent execution and spending after cancellation arrives.
The interval between signal delivery and wait_latched detecting it leaves the launch boundary open.
The real-signal tests keep the signalling child asleep and do not cover another worker launching during the polling interval; the claimed mutation walk does not establish that missing property.
The lifecycle changes fit the stated scope and introduce no unnecessary flags or compatibility machinery.
The delta introduces no irreversible migration; rollback remains local to the runner and its tests.
Report-only and regrade now refresh integrity and reject mismatched manifests as unknown; cancellation visibility still overstates launch prevention.
The claim that no run starts after an interrupt is stronger than the implemented polling-based cancellation.
The model-spawn guard checks stop and interrupted events, but neither reflects a newly latched signal until the main thread processes it.
No quoted contract is weakened. Regression tests accompany the changes, but omit the cancellation ordering failure identified here.
